{{short description|Irish academic leader, founder and first president of Dublin City University}}
{{Use dmy dates|date=June 2020}}
{{Use Irish English|date=June 2020}}
'''Daniel O'Hare''', often Danny O'Hare,<ref name="DCUPP">{{cite web |title=Past Presidents of DCU |url=https://www.dcu.ie/president/past-presidents-of-dcu.shtml |website=Dublin City University |date=3 May 2013 |accessdate=14 August 2018}}</ref> (born 1942), is an [[Irish people|Irish]] academic and former university leader, best known as the founding leader and first president of [[Dublin City University]], one of two new universities established in [[Republic of Ireland|Ireland]] in September 1989.<ref name="IT_DCU">{{cite news |last1=Byrne (compiler) |first1=Anne |title=Factfile: Dublin City University |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/education/factfile-dublin-city-university-1.1046750 |accessdate=14 August 2018 |publisher=The Irish Times Trust |date=15 Jan 2002}}</ref>  He has also held a wide range of public governance positions, and is an elected Member of the [[Royal Irish Academy]] in the Science division.<ref name="RIAProfile">{{cite web |title=RIA - Members - Daniel O'Hare |url=https://www.ria.ie/daniel-ohare |website=The Royal Irish Academy |date=19 October 2015 |accessdate=14 August 2018}}</ref>  Coming from [[Dundalk]],<ref name="DCUPP"/> he is a chemist, specialized in advanced spectroscopy.

==Life==
===Early life===
O'Hare was born in [[County Louth]], growing up in [[Dundalk]], where he attended the local Christian Brothers School<ref name="MedCclPrf">{{cite web |title=Medical Council (of Ireland) - Members - Daniel O'Hare |url=http://medicalcouncil.newsweaver.co.uk/MedicalCouncil/n8loejv8mxb |website=The Medical Council (of Ireland) |accessdate=14 August 2018 |archive-date=14 August 2018 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20180814135154/http://medicalcouncil.newsweaver.co.uk/MedicalCouncil/n8loejv8mxb |url-status=dead }}</ref> until 1960.<ref name="ITNIHEPrf">{{cite news |last1=Mercator |title=People in business - NIHE conscious of the need to fit into the community |newspaper=The Irish Times |publisher=The Irish Times Trust |date=7 April 1986 |page=14}}</ref>

===Academic career===
O'Hare graduated from [[University College Galway]] (UCG),<ref name="DCUPP"/> now NUI Galway, where he qualified with a BSc in Chemistry, and then an MSc in Organic Chemistry.<ref name="DCUPP"/> He took a post as an assistant at UCG from 1964 to 1965.<ref name="DCUPP"/> He later studied for a Ph.D. at the University of St Andrews in Scotland, working with gas-phase ultraviolet spectroscopy, and qualifying in 1968.<ref name="DCUPP"/><ref name="ITNIHEPrf"/>

O'Hare took up an assistant professorship at [[Michigan State University]], before moving to the [[University of Southampton]] as a research fellow for a year.<ref name="ITNIHEPrf"/>

===RTC Letterkenny, RTC Waterford===
O'Hare was appointed in 1971 as the first principal of Regional Technical College, [[Letterkenny]], now [[Letterkenny Institute of Technology]], serving until 1974, before becoming the second head of Regional Technical College, [[Waterford]], now [[Waterford Institute of Technology]].<ref name="ITNIHEPrf"/>

===NIHE Dublin and DCU President===
O'Hare took up a role as the director of the to-be National Institute of Higher Education Dublin in 1977, working from a city centre office,<ref name="IT_DCU"/> while plans, and a campus, for the new institution were worked on.  He oversaw the NIHE until 1989, when he led its conversion to university status, on the same day as the [[University of Limerick]].  He and his team secured funding from both international and national sources, including philanthropists such as [[Chuck Feeney]].  The NIHE and DCU focused on blending the needs of academia and industry,<ref name="IT_Self_Bus">{{cite news |last1=O'Hare |first1=Daniel (Danny) |title=Universities promise innovation to industry |newspaper=The Irish Times |publisher=The Irish Times Trust |date=4 March 1994 |page=14}}</ref> including a [[cooperative education]] system, INTRA.

O'Hare announced in November 1998 that he would step down in September 1999.<ref name="ITDepNt">{{cite news |last1=Pollak |first1=Andy |title=O'Hare to leave DCU in 1999 |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/o-hare-to-leave-dcu-in-1999-1.216654 |accessdate=14 August 2018 |publisher=The Irish Times |date=20 November 1998}}</ref>

==Consultant roles==
O'Hare has been a consultant to the [[World Bank]] and the [[OECD]].<ref name="MedCclPrf"/>

==Other roles==
O'Hare has chaired the [[Conference of Heads of Irish Universities]]<ref name="ITDepNt"/> and the national coordinating body for distance education of adults, an area in which DCU specialised.<ref name="IT_Nov96_FSB_RTC">{{cite news |last1=O'Connor |first1=Alison |title=Hoping to find the right recipe |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/hoping-to-find-the-right-recipe-1.104148 |access-date=21 January 2021 |work=Irish Times |date=9 November 1996}}</ref>  During his time at DCU, he was also asked to chair a local project coordination body, [[Dublin City Council]]'s Ballymun Regeneration Ltd., overseeing the more than a billion euro investment in renewing much of the residential provision for the area, as well as provision of new civic facilities,<ref name="ITDepNt"/> and, from 1994, the Board of nearby [[Beaumont Hospital, Dublin|Beaumont Hospital]].  In 1996, he was appointed by the government as the founding chairperson of the [[Food Safety Authority of Ireland]],<ref name="ITDepNt"/> overseeing staffing, establishment of its legislative basis and mission definition.<ref name="IT_Nov96_FSB_RTC"/>  He also led Ireland's Expert Group on Future Skills Needs and Task Force on the Physical Sciences, and the Information Society Commission.  After his time at DCU, O'Hare also chaired the governing body of the [[Milltown Institute of Theology and Philosophy]]<ref name="MedCclPrf"/> and the Dublin Airport Stakeholders Forum.<ref name="MedCclPrf"/>

He has been a member of the [[Medical Council (Ireland)|Medical Council]] of Ireland, from 2008-2013,<ref name="MedCcl_AnnRpt2010">{{cite book |title=Annual Report 2010 |date=2011 |publisher=Medical Council of Ireland |location=Dublin, Ireland |page=9}}</ref> and 2013-2018, where he chaired the Fitness to Practice Committee and was a member of several other committees.<ref name="MedCclPrf"/>  He also sat on the boards of the [[Edmund Rice Schools Trust]], the Daughters of Charity, Digitary, Music Generation, [[Media Lab Europe]], and Calor Gas.<ref name="MedCclPrf"/>

===Exploration Station===
O'Hare promoted, and is chair of the board of, the interactive National Children's Science Centre project, also known as ''Exploration Station'',<ref name="IT_NSSC">{{cite news |last1=Reville |first1=William |title=Dedicated Followers of Fission (National Children's Science Centre) |url=https://www.irishtimes.com/news/science/dedicated-followers-of-fission-1.3310994 |accessdate=14 August 2018 |publisher=The Irish Times |date=30 November 2017}}</ref><ref name="MedCclPrf"/> which planned to open its new educational facility in 2020.<ref name="IT_NSSC"/>

==Memberships and recognition==
O'Hare is a Member of the [[Royal Irish Academy]], elected in the Science division in 1999.<ref name="DOH_RIA">{{cite web |title=Daniel O'Hare |url=https://www.ria.ie/daniel-ohare |website=Royal Irish Academy |date=19 October 2015 |access-date=2 February 2021}}</ref>

He holds honorary doctorates from the [[University of Dublin]] (1992), [[University of Ulster]] (1994), [[Queen's University, Belfast]] (1995), the [[National University of Ireland]] (1999),<ref name="DCUPP"/> and DCU (2008).<ref name="RIAProfile"/>

==Personal life==
O'Hare is married to Sheelagh (née Kenny) from Galway, and they have four children, Michael, Nicholas, Domhnall and Fiona.<ref name="ITNIHEPrf"/>
